raj: pulling edge traces now. I can see route flapping between us-west1-pop02 -> us-west2-pop03 for ~1200 flows, TTL jump + path change. Looks like DNS glue is returning alternating anycast egress.

support-bot: suggested repro command posted to customer.

jess: they ran it — direct to pop02 handshake ~40ms, but normal DNS route shows 600-900ms for ClientHello -> ServerHello, p99 ~1.1s.
matt: I ran a quick traceroute from our egress tester to the affected pop, see hop 5 -> core-az-b with 320ms. Suspicious. Posting output:
```
traceroute to us-west1-pop02 (34.201.12.77), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  1.1 ms
 2  core-az-a  5.2 ms
 3  core-az-b  320 ms  <--- jump
 4  us-west1-pop02  35.5 ms
```
raj: that interconnect hop 3 looks like a transient routing detour. Could explain TLS handshake RTT inflation because ClientHello retransmits during long SYN/TLS timeouts.
elaine: mitigation idea: force fallback routing policy to prefer same-az egress for existing sessions for 15m while network team investigates. Anyone object?
jess: do it, customers are on the line. Add a canary to avoid global churn. :thumbsup:

raj: monitoring now — within 5m p95 dropped from 450ms -> 110ms, p99 dropped from 1.1s -> 350ms for affected customer set.
